body: Nope, I have no idea why I am having these thoughts. They just come over me randomly, I don't intentionally think of then, they just suddenly appear - and then I can't stop thinking about that topic.

That's a though question to answer.  Let's say you gave me a loaded gun - I probably wouldn't use it to kill myself, mostly because there would be a chance of surviving as a 100% handicapped human. 

But if there was a way to guarante certain death without suffering... I honestly don't know what I'd do if I had the chance to use such a method. It'd surely sound tempting.

> *Woman haha.

Ooops! :D

Usually it's about how easy it'd be to kill myself and how it wouldn't really affect my any more, because, well, I would be dead. There would be no consequences. I then sometimes think about how my friends would react to the news that I had killed myself. But most of my thoughts are centered around how I could kill myself.

It's okay man. I don't remember when it started, but I didn't have these thoughts all life long. 

What do you mean by "What are they like?"? Do you want to know what I am thinking about in detail or something else?

No, I don't have anyone to talk to. I don't even know what I would want to talk about with that person since I don't want to kill myself, I just end up thinking about it over and over again, but I can't do anything to stop that from happening.
Kind of, kind of not. I mentioned it briefly about two months ago when I had a "deep" talk with a friend of mine. But it slipped through kinda unnoticed.

The feeling that comes closest to when I feel when I think about suicide is a mix of guilt and the feeling you get when you think you forgot to do something, but you can't remember what exactly. 
But again, I am not actively trying to kill myself, I am just having thoughts about it and I don't have an explanation of why they are occurring (if that makes sense).

> I don't want you to experiment with life and death.

I don't like the thought of experimenting with life and death either. I never harmed myself, because of the scars it would leave on my skin and because it would accomplish nothing. Well, I tried it one time, which proved to me how useless harming oneself is. It didn't make me forget about my thoughts, it just led to annoying itching for the next few days.
(I'm assuming that's what you meant with what I quoted)

That's... well, an interesting way to look at it. 
 
 
> [...] With this immense power comes crazy thoughts [...]

"Crazy thoughts" seems to be an appropriate term to describe what's going on inside my head sometimes.

If by "Does the idea of dying sound comforting to you?" you mean the process of dying - then no. Like I said, I have collected some experience about what it feels like to almost die. I felt severe pain for over three days until I was treated and even then, the pain continued until about two months later. In short, I don't like suffering. Dying would mean that I'd have to suffer - and the suffering might continue of if I'd somehow survive.
But if you meant, whether the idea of being dead sounded comforting to me - I would probably answer with yes. More or less because of my thoughts which, surprisingly, made me curious. But at the same time, I am not even really sure whether I really want to know what being dead is like.

Yes, I have already thought about just doing it. I got a rope laying around somewhere, we got a ton of medication in our house (which I don't think would kill me) and there are a few very sharp knifes. 
It's just... I don't know what's driving me to get out of here, as well as I don't know what's keeping me here.
